text:
sarah: Heads-up: prod svc `gpu-infer.us-west2` is spiking retries. One endpoint in gpu-node-pool-b is getting ~60-70% of connections, other endpoints nearly idle. Observed RDMA negotiation errors + increased packet loss. Anyone awake?

alim: on it, seeing latency + packet drops on east-west within that AZ. Grafana shows qps concentrated to pod gpu-infer-7c9d on node gpu-03. GPU utilization pegged, queue buildup.

ops-bot: Incident INC-4571 created (severity: high) by sarah. Playbook: infra/networking/kubeproxy-ipvs.md

alan: quick checks: `kubectl get endpoints svc/gpu-infer -o wide` returns all endpoints Ready, but kube-proxy IPVS stats show skewed connection counts. pushing ipvs dump now.

tomas: dropping the ipvs snapshot here — looks like some persistent conn entries pinned to a single backend (maybe stale hash).

zhen: ```
# ipvsadm -ln --exact
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.3.12.45:8080 rr
  -> 10.2.8.21:8080               Masq    1      1883       0
  -> 10.2.9.11:8080               Masq    1       23       0
  -> 10.2.10.7:8080               Masq    1       15       0
```

zhen: see ActiveConn 1883 on 10.2.8.21 (gpu-03). That matches the GPU hot node.

alim: also ran `tcpdump -i bond0 -n host 10.2.8.21 and port 8080` — lots of retransmits and MTU-related fragmentation warnings. RDMA logs on node show `ib_core` errors.

sarah: suspect either endpoint weight calc is broken (ipvs hash collision) or hairpin/stickiness due to conn reuse with IPVS NAT + RDMA fallback. Any node-level kernel changes recently?

zhen: kube-proxy was rolled last night (v1.26.3->v1.26.4) with a patch to conntrack reclaiming. Could be related.

alim: quick mitigation plan: 1) restart kube-proxy on two kubelets in that AZ (gpu-03, gpu-05) to clear ipvs maps; 2) cordon+drain the overloaded gpu-03 and shift pods; 3) temporarily set service externalTrafficPolicy=Local? (no, that's for external LB). Alternative: force endpoints reshuffle by patching endpoints object (not ideal).

ops-bot: deploy-bot queued restart of kube-proxy on nodes [gpu-03 gpu-05] (canary).

deploy-bot: kube-proxy restart started on gpu-03 (step 1/2).

tomas: after restart, ipvs ActiveConn distribution looks better: 10.2.8.21 dropped from 1883->120. Still some retransmits but much lower.

sarah: gpu-03 still showing intermittent RDMA errors in dmesg. Suggest we cordon and fully evict to test whether traffic rebalances and RDMA errors stop. That will force scheduling to other nodes and remove any node-local kernel state.

alim: cordon+drain gpu-03 now. Eviction succeeded, pods moved to gpu-01/gpu-04.

zhen: post-drain ipvs snapshot: ActiveConn now spread across backends ~430/380/360. Packet loss and retransmits dropped to baseline. RDMA errors stopped on gpu-03 (no longer receiving traffic).

sarah: root cause hypothesis: kube-proxy IPVS map had stuck/persistent connection entries (hash affinity + conntrack interplay) that biased new connections toward a single backend. Kernel/rdma stack exposed MTU mismatch / packet loss under load, which then amplified retries and GPU queueing. Rollout of kube-proxy last night likely triggered map rebuilds exposing the issue.

alim: next steps: 1) run `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward` and verify MTU across NICs and SR-IOV/RDMA paths; 2) schedule canary of kube-proxy v1.26.4 on a small pool with extra conntrack tuning; 3) add health-check to detect single-endpoint >50% connection skew and auto-restart kube-proxy there.

zhen: logging the commands we used: ```
kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/kube-proxy --tail=200 | grep ipvs
ipvsadm -ln --exact
ss -tn sport = :8080 state established | wc -l
ethtool -i eth0
```

ops-bot: Action items recorded on INC-4571: [restart kube-proxy canary] [conntrack tuning RFC] [endpoint-skew monitor] [postmortem due EOD].

sarah: cost note: overloaded node caused queued requests and retries that drove up GPU minutes by ~13% in that AZ last hour. We'll include that in the postmortem as ops cost impact.

tomas: for now incident is mitigated (traffic balanced, RDMA errors stopped). Keeping incident open for monitoring window 2h. Reopen if skew returns. :thumbsup:

alim: leaving a small follow-up: we should add an ipvs map scrub at kube-proxy startup and a check in CI for conntrack/ipvs interplay. I'll draft PR after postmortem.

sarah: thanks all. Closing notes will go to #postmortems once we complete the write-up.
